posts.title: Does your business need a website or just a social media page?
posts.excerpt: A social media page is a great start, but it is not the same as owning your online home. Here is an honest way to decide what you need right now.
posts.body_markdown:
Almost every small shop starts online with a Facebook page, and that makes sense. It is free, your customers are already there and you can post a new product in two minutes. So do you really need a website? The honest answer is: it depends on how you sell and where you want to go.

## What a Facebook page does well

- **Reach.** Most of your local customers scroll Facebook every day.
- **Conversation.** Messenger makes it easy to answer questions and close a sale.
- **Low cost.** You can start today with no budget.

If you sell a few products, mostly to people nearby, and you are happy taking orders by inbox, a well-managed Facebook page may be enough for now.

## Where a Facebook page falls short

- **You do not own it.** If your page is restricted, hacked or the algorithm changes, your reach can drop overnight.
- **Posts get buried.** A customer looking for a product you posted three months ago has to scroll and scroll. Many give up.
- **Orders are messy.** Inbox orders, screenshots and handwritten notes are easy to lose, especially during a big sale.
- **Google does not show it well.** When someone searches "custom furniture near me" or "math tutoring in my city", a proper website has a much better chance of appearing.
- **Trust.** Bigger buyers, corporate clients and foreign customers often check for a website before they call.

## A simple way to decide

Ask yourself these questions:

1. Do customers often ask for your full price list or catalogue?
2. Do you lose track of orders or payments?
3. Do you want customers from outside your area, or from Google?
4. Do you deal with companies, institutions or buyers abroad?

If you answered yes to one or two, a simple business website (5–7 pages, contact form, WhatsApp button and map) will help. If you answered yes to most, and you sell products online regularly, an e-commerce store with online payments and order management will save you time every single day.

## You do not have to choose one

The best setup for most shops is both. Use Facebook to reach people and start conversations, and use your website as the place where they see everything clearly, trust you and place an order. Every Facebook post can link back to the right product page.

## Start small

You do not need a big budget to begin. A starter business website can be ready in one to two weeks, and you can upgrade to an admin panel or a full store later. The important thing is to own a place online that is yours.

Not sure which option fits your shop? Message us on WhatsApp and describe how you sell today. We will give you an honest recommendation, even if the answer is "your Facebook page is enough for now".

posts.title: What a coaching center management system actually saves you
posts.excerpt: Beyond the buzzwords: the real hours, money and stress a simple management system can save a coaching center every month.
posts.body_markdown:
If you run a coaching center, you know the real work starts after class. Who has paid this month? Who missed three classes in a row? Which batch has a free seat? Which guardian needs a call? Most centers answer these questions with registers, Excel sheets and memory. A management system does not replace teaching, but it can take a lot of that weight off your shoulders.

We are building our own School & Coaching Management System and testing it in a real classroom, so these are lessons from daily use, not a sales brochure.

## 1. Time spent on fee collection

At the start of each month, someone goes through the register to find who has paid and who has not. With a system, dues are calculated automatically. You open one screen and see every unpaid student by batch. You can send an SMS reminder to all guardians with dues in a single step instead of making call after call.

## 2. Money lost to missed fees

When records live on paper, some fees are simply forgotten, especially when a student joins mid-month or changes batch. Even a few missed fees each month add up over a year. A system that tracks every student and every payment closes those gaps.

## 3. Attendance headaches

Marking attendance on paper is quick, but finding patterns is not. A system can show you which students are absent often, so you can talk to them or their guardians before they drop out. Keeping students is always cheaper than finding new ones.

## 4. Results and guardian communication

Preparing exam results by hand and sharing them one by one takes hours. With results stored in the system, you can publish them quickly and send an SMS to guardians. Parents notice when a center communicates clearly, and that builds your reputation.

## 5. Your own peace of mind

This is the saving people talk about least but feel the most. When all your records are in one place and backed up, you are not afraid of losing a register or a laptop. You can check how your center is doing from your phone, even when you are not there.

## What it costs

A good system should not be a big burden. Our School & Coaching System is priced at $99 per month, which covers students, batches, attendance, fees, SMS and results. For many centers, recovering just one or two missed fees a month covers the cost.

## Is it right for you?

If you have more than one batch, more than a few dozen students, or you spend hours every month chasing fees, a management system will likely pay for itself. If you are just starting with a handful of students, a register may still be fine, and that is okay too.

Want to see how it works? Message us on WhatsApp and we will show you a demo and answer your questions.

posts.title: How to brief a software agency so you get the right price
posts.excerpt: Vague requests lead to vague quotes. A short, clear brief helps any agency give you an accurate price and timeline. Here is what to include.
posts.body_markdown:
"How much does a website cost?" is one of the most common questions we receive. It is a fair question, but it is a bit like asking "How much does a house cost?" The answer depends on what you need. The good news is that you do not need technical knowledge to get an accurate quote. You only need to explain your business clearly.

Here is a simple brief you can prepare in 15 minutes and send to any agency, including us.

## 1. Tell us about your business

Write two or three lines: what you sell, who your customers are and where you operate. For example: "We sell stainless steel kitchen racks and railings, mostly to home owners and builders."

## 2. Describe the problem, not just the solution

Instead of only saying "I need an app", explain what is not working today. "Our sales staff take 20 minutes to prepare each quotation" or "We lose track of inbox orders during sales" tells an agency much more. Sometimes the right solution is smaller and cheaper than you expected.

## 3. List the must-have features

Keep this list short and honest. Separate what you need on day one from what would be nice later. For an online store, must-haves might be: product catalogue, cart, online payments and order management. Nice-to-haves might be: coupons, a mobile app or customer reviews.

## 4. Share examples you like

Send links to two or three websites or apps you like, and say what you like about them: the colours, the simple layout, the way products are shown. This saves a lot of back-and-forth.

## 5. Mention your content

Who will provide text, product photos, prices and logo? If you already have them, say so. If you need help, mention it. Missing content is one of the most common reasons projects get delayed.

## 6. Be open about budget and deadline

Many owners hide their budget, worried they will be overcharged. In practice, sharing a range helps a good agency suggest the best option within it. If you have a real deadline, such as a launch date or a busy season, mention it early.

## 7. Ask the right questions back

When you receive a quote, check:

- What exactly is included, and what is not?
- How long will it take, and how will I see progress?
- What happens after launch? Is there free support?
- Who owns the domain, hosting and code?
- How is payment split?

At Meghbyte, every quote lists the features, the timeline and the payment terms in writing. Small projects are paid 50% in advance and 50% before handover, larger ones by milestone, and every project includes 30 days of free bug fixing after launch.

## A short brief beats a long meeting

A few clear paragraphs by email or WhatsApp are enough to start. Send us your brief and we will reply with questions, suggestions and an honest quote.

# Privacy Policy

*Last updated: October 2026*

Meghbyte ("we", "us") respects your privacy. This policy explains what information we collect through our quote form and how we use it.

## Information we collect

When you submit the quote form, we store:

- Your name
- Your phone number
- Your email address
- Your business name
- Your message

We only collect the information you choose to send us.

## How we use your information

We use this information only to reply to your enquiry, discuss your project and send you a quote. We do not use it for advertising, and we do not sell, rent or share it with third parties, except where required by law.

## Cookies and tracking

Our website does not use tracking or advertising cookies. We may use cookies that are strictly necessary for the website to work, such as keeping the form secure.

## How long we keep it

We keep your enquiry only as long as needed to respond and to keep a record of our conversation about your project.

## Your rights

You can ask us to show, correct or delete your information at any time. To request deletion, message us on WhatsApp at **+880 1890-827598** and we will remove your data.

We take reasonable steps to protect your information from unauthorised access, loss or misuse.
